articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Tuesday condemned the attack on a commercial vessel off Oman’s coast that left one Indian national
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Tuesday condemned the attack on a commercial vessel off Oman’s coast that left one Indian national dead and 13 others rescued. The vessel, MSV Al Jusufi, came under attack near Limah on Monday evening.In a statement, the MEA said the Indian national died after sustaining injuries in the attack. It conveyed its condolences to the family of the deceased and said the Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the situation.The embassy is coordinating with Omani authorities to facilitate the early repatriation of the 13 rescued Indian nationals as well as the mortal remains of the deceased, the ministry said.Expressing concern over repeated attacks on commercial shipping in the region, the MEA called for an immediate de-escalation of tensions and the conclusion of ongoing negotiations to reach a diplomatic solution."The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end," the statement said, adding that free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored in accordance with international law.The ministry reiterated that peace and stability in the region could return only through diplomatic efforts and an end to attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure.The deceased seafarer has been identified as Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, who succumbed to his injuries while the remaining 13 crew members were safely evacuated and rescued by the Omani Coast Guard.Sharing details of the incident in a post on X, Sonowal said the vessel, MSV AL JUSUFI, was hit by the unidentified aerial object on November 2.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Dilip Ghosh takes 'Sonia' jibe at Mamata for joining INDIA bloc rally against SIR
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Taking a dig at Mamata, he said that she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for leadership out of "utter helplessness".Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.“Earlier, she set out to become the top leader herself. Now, she has nothing left in her hands. Today, she isn’t even an elected representative. That is why, out of utter helplessness, she goes around accepting Sonia ji as her leader again. Her party is finished today,” news agency ANI reported, quoting Ghosh.He also hit out at Banerjee over her objections to the electoral process, saying political parties must respect the people's mandate. He alleged that she had no complaints about the Election Commission or democracy when her party was winning elections.“As long as she was winning, democracy was fine, and the Election Commission was fine. The moment she lost, everything went wrong. Keep faith in the people; the people decide who wins and who loses. One must accept the verdict of the public,” he said.The minister further claimed that the removal of fake voters during the electoral roll revision had paved the way for free and fair elections in West Bengal. He alleged that Banerjee had benefited from such voters in previous elections.“Look, when the revision occurred, the fake voter base through which Mamata used to win was eliminated. Once they were separated, a free and fair election took place. A genuine election happened in Bengal after many years, and people are happy about it; change has arrived. No outsider can simply enter and become a citizen of this country or avail benefits here,” he said.Ghosh also said the ruling government and party workers would organise rallies across the state to counter the Opposition's attempts to create unrest and communicate their position to the public.“It is also our responsibility to make people understand and deliver the right message. The people are nationalist, and the government is nationalist. No one will be permitted to create unrest in the country. We will also reach out to the people and hold rallies everywhere; this is just the beginning,” he said.Festive season security arrangementsMeanwhile, Ghosh said the state government was making arrangements to ensure that Deepavali, Kali Puja and Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations passed off peacefully.He said every cabinet minister had been assigned a district to oversee law and order during the festive season. Ghosh has been given responsibility for Purba Medinipur, also known as East Midnapore.“The government is keeping a close watch across all of West Bengal to ensure that the upcoming Deepavali, Kali Puja, and Jagaddhatri Puja are conducted smoothly and with enthusiasm. Every cabinet minister has been assigned the responsibility of overseeing law and order in one district. I have been given charge of Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore). I am also meeting with them to ensure all arrangements are in place and nothing goes wrong. This is the government’s duty, and the public must cooperate,” he said.Ghosh targets Mamata over development boardsThe minister also criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government over the functioning of development boards set up for marginalised communities, including the Matua community.He alleged that several boards formed during Banerjee's tenure had not received adequate funds or been given meaningful work.“Mamata Banerjee had formed several development boards in West Bengal: the Rajbanshi Board, the Matua Board, the Bhumij Adivasi Board, but gave neither funds nor work to anyone. She only played politics,” he said.Ghosh said the Matua community, many of whose members migrated from Bangladesh, continued to face economic hardships and needed focused development measures. He said the board should be made functional and provided with funds.“Now, for that community, especially the Matua community, most of whom came from Bangladesh, have numerous hardships and are poor. Their development must happen; therefore, the board must be actively functional for them, and funds must be provided, which our chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) has initiated," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
